title: Testing an interpretation through anomalous results
shortTitle: Testing an interpretation through anomalous results
summary: An absurdity or anomaly argument evaluates whether a proposed interpretation produces consequences incompatible with the statutory scheme or intended operation.
notes:
Raila compares a pedestrian struck by a delivered parcel with one struck by the same postal truck, and liquid spilled from a parcel with water left by a janitor. The panel regarded immunity distinctions based on those differences as inconsistent with the statutory purpose and used them to test the government’s reading.

These are explanatory hypotheticals, not facts found in Raila. Katzmann also notes that the threshold for disregarding clear text as absurd is a demanding and contested question; disfavored consequences alone do not establish permission to rewrite a law. The case’s contextual use of anomalies should therefore be distinguished from a freestanding power to correct any undesirable policy.
